title: Canonical base-change maps on the universal rank condition
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $E$ be finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], $g:T\to S$, and assume $R(f,E,g)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-rank-match]. For every $h:T'\to T$, the two canonical ordinary module base-change maps [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction] for $p_g:X\times_S T\to T$ and the modules $q_g^*E$ and $q_g^*(E^\vee)$ are isomorphisms. The square is the categorical pullback of $p_g$ along $h$. No structure-sheaf unit hypothesis is required and no representing scheme is asserted.

proof.text: Work on common-rank neighbourhoods of T. Perfect derived direct images with arbitrary base change have local finite-free models starting in degree zero. Universal rank matching implies the rank-r lowest-cohomology condition on these neighbourhoods and on every further test scheme.

Factor each neighbourhood through the lowest-cohomology rank-r locus. The residue-field tests give lowest fibre dimension r at the image points. Choose the residue models used in Tag 0BDL, cancelling contractible summands so that the first term has rank r and there are no negative terms. On the locus the outgoing degree-zero matrix in this chosen model is zero, so H^0 is the first free term. Every further scalar extension leaves that matrix zero. The canonical degree-zero cohomology base-change morphism is the identity on this scalar extension, hence an isomorphism for E and for its dual. Identify this morphism with the ordinary adjoint-defined moduleBaseChangeMap by naturality of degree-zero direct-image comparison and the adjunction triangle identities; an arbitrary object isomorphism does not suffice.

Open restriction compares these canonical maps with those in the restricted squares. Isomorphisms of sheaves can be checked on the common-rank open cover, so the local invertibility proves both global claims. Rank zero is zero-to-zero; empty schemes impose no point conditions.

theorem picardRankMatch_baseChange {X S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E : X.Modules) [E.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (g : T ⟶ S)
    (hR : PicardUniversalRankMatch f E g) :
  ∀ {T' : Scheme.{u}} (h : T' ⟶ T),
    IsIso (Modules.moduleBaseChangeMap (pullback.snd f g)
      (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f g) h) h (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f g) h)
      pullback.condition ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj E)) ∧
    IsIso (Modules.moduleBaseChangeMap (pullback.snd f g)
      (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f g) h) h (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f g) h)
      pullback.condition ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj (Modules.dual E)))
